arcs.title: Dana and the basil cups
arcs.stage: 4/5 — her number is in his phone; Sun Nov 8 two leaves on his cup and a good-luck 'drive it home'. He took a photo of Moshe Sunday night but did not send it (the deal is a week). Next: the photo about Sat Nov 14, then a first date.

arcs.title: Saving Moshe
arcs.stage: 2/3 — recovering on the kitchen counter by the sink, tops pinched, Dana's small unnamed sprout beside him. Next: new leaves, then thriving.

arcs.title: Gadi and the chickpea logo
arcs.stage: Invoice sent Sun Nov 8 at thirty days (Gadi wanted sixty). Today 10:00: the video presentation; the client asks for something extra and Ishai answers with improv's 'yes, and' and a price. Next: the extra version and getting paid.

arcs.title: Noa, the best friend
arcs.stage: Coached him Sunday (blue shirt). Today she waits for the result and texts at lunch. Next: she'll want him to come to the Pump House or celebrate.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Lesson 1 done; homework done with Lior. Today 'yes, and' shows up for real in the presentation. Next: lesson 2 Thu Nov 12 at 17:00, then a beer with Tomer.

arcs.title: The wider circle
arcs.stage: Tomer fixed the hallway light; Mrs. Levi approves of him. Today: Avi at the kiosk, Sivan and Michal at the gym for the first real chat, Tomer by phone hears about the Penguins can Fly poster. Next: Mr. Zelig, Kobi, Boaz's poker invitation (Nov 19-21).

beats.goal: In the blue shirt at his desk, Ishai presents the chickpea logo on a video call with Gadi and the client (Ruti, camera off; Gadi relays her). She loves it but asks if the chickpea can wink for the app. Ishai almost apologises, then says 'yes, and' and offers a winking version as a paid extra. Gadi is stunned and agrees to 1,000 more.
beats.teaser: Ishai presents the chickpea logo live on a video call at 10:00
beats.forceText: At his desk in the blue shirt, Ishai finishes the chickpea presentation on a video call and closes the laptop with both hands.

forceLines.say: She wants it to wink. A small thing. For the app.
Yes. And a winking version is a thousand more.

forceCommentary.say: He said a number. Out loud. To Gadi. I need to sit down.
The chickpea winks. The invoice does not.

moments.text: Ishai sits at the desk in a pressed blue shirt and pyjama trousers, the laptop open on the video call, the chickpea logo filling the shared screen. Falafel lies on his feet under the desk.

lines.say: You're on. Ruti is here, camera off. She's eating, don't take it personally.
Good morning, Ruti. Thank you for... okay. I'll start.
This is the chickpea. Rounder than before. Friendlier eyebrows.
She says 'friendlier eyebrows' is a sentence she never expected to hear.
The old one looked worried. Like it owed money.
She laughed. Keep going, keep going.
The leaf on top is the brand. It works small, on a lid, on a sticker.
She's asking what font. Don't say the font has feelings.
It's round and heavy. It sits like someone who isn't in a hurry.
That's feelings, Ishai. She liked it. Next slide.

commentary.say: Blue shirt on top, pyjamas below. The duality of the freelance man.
Friendlier eyebrows. Somewhere a chickpea is finally at peace.

moments.text: Ishai clicks to the last slide: the logo on a jar, a bag and a phone icon. He leans in to listen, then stops with his mouth half open.

lines.say: Small thing. Ruti asks: can the chickpea wink? On the phone icon. Small.
Oh. Sorry, I didn't... I mean...
Is that a no? She's waiting.
No. Wait. Yes.
Yes, and the wink becomes a tiny animation. It winks when the order is ready.
She put her sandwich down. She never puts her sandwich down.
Three frames. Eyes, half closed, wink. It feels like a friend saying 'done'.
She says she wants it. When?
Thursday morning. And it's a separate job. A small one, but separate.
...She says fine. Who are you today?

commentary.say: He almost said sorry and then said YES AND. Yael, take a bow.
The client put down her sandwich. In this industry that's a standing ovation.

moments.text: The client has left the call. Gadi's voice stays on the line while Ishai stares at his own face in the small video window.

lines.say: She's gone. What was that? Since when do you sell things?
I have a class on Thursdays. They make you say yes.
They should make you say cheaper. How much is the wink?
Twelve hundred.
Eight. It's three frames, Ishai. Three.
Three frames she'll see every day. A thousand.
A thousand. And I'm telling everyone you've become difficult.
Tell them I've become... available on Thursday morning.
Very funny. Send the files Wednesday night. Good job. Don't get used to it.
You said good job first. Before anything else.

commentary.say: Gadi said 'good job' before asking for something. Mark the date.
Twelve hundred, settled at a thousand. That's a man who's done his homework.

update.memory: Ishai sold the client a winking chickpea for 1,000 extra on the call, straight out of nowhere. Says his Thursday class taught him. Files due Wednesday night.

moments.text: Ishai closes the laptop, stands up, raises both arms and spins once. Falafel barks. He goes to the counter and bends down to Moshe and the sprout.

lines.say: A thousand. For a wink. Moshe, I said a number.
Don't tell Dana. I'll tell her. In a week.

commentary.say: He's reporting to the basil first. Noa is going to be furious.
Moshe received the news calmly. As a professional.

beats.goal: Ishai treats himself to falafel at Avi's kiosk, still in the blue shirt. Avi thinks he's going to a wedding, hears about the wink and gives him a proverb. It's Sigd; Avi's neighbour went to Jerusalem for it at dawn (one mention). Noa texts demanding the result; Ishai answers out loud while Avi listens in.
beats.teaser: Ishai celebrates at Avi's kiosk, and Noa wants answers
beats.forceText: At Avi's kiosk Ishai eats a falafel in the blue shirt while typing a long text to Noa with one thumb.

forceLines.say: Blue shirt on a Monday, champion? Who's getting married?
Nobody. A chickpea winked and I got paid.

forceCommentary.say: Celebrating a chickpea with a chickpea. The circle of life.

moments.text: Lunchtime on Herzl Street, cold and bright. Ishai stands at Avi's kiosk in the blue shirt under his jacket; Avi stuffs a pita and stops halfway to look at him.

lines.say: Champion! A blue shirt on a Monday. Who's getting married?
Nobody. I had a presentation. A video call.
On video you wear a shirt. Below?
Below is my business, Avi.
Ha! So it went well. I see it in your face. Extra amba?
Extra everything. The client asked for a chickpea that winks.
A chickpea that winks. Like my falafel. Every ball winks at you.
And I told them it costs extra. And they said yes.
Listen to me. The man who names his price eats with both hands.
I'm eating with both hands. Look.
My neighbour Tsega went to Jerusalem for Sigd at five this morning. You celebrate here.
Then this is my little Jerusalem. With amba.

commentary.say: Avi saw the shirt and assumed a wedding. Avi, keep that energy for Dana.
'The man who names his price eats with both hands.' Avi has never charged the same twice.

message.say: WELL??? I've been staring at my phone since ten. Did you say sorry? How many times? Numbers, Ishush.

moments.text: Ishai's phone buzzes on the counter next to the pita. He reads it, smiles and types with one thumb while Avi leans over the counter to see.

lines.say: Noa. She wants numbers. Zero sorrys. One almost.
Who is this Noa? The coffee girl?
No. Noa is my friend since forever. The coffee girl is Dana.
Two girls. And a chickpea. Busy man.
It's not like that. Noa tells me to raise my prices.
Then marry her. A woman who tells you to charge more is gold.
Avi, I'm writing to her now. Stop reading over my shoulder.
I'm not reading. I'm adding tahini. Write 'a thousand extra'.
I wrote 'a thousand extra'. With three exclamation marks.
Three? Two is confidence. Three is surprise. Delete one.
I'm leaving three. I am surprised.

commentary.say: Avi is now his PR department. And his marriage counsellor.
Two exclamation marks is confidence. Three is surprise. Write that on a mug.

update.memory: Ishai came in a blue shirt after a presentation: the client paid extra for a winking chickpea. He has Noa, who pushes his prices, and Dana, the coffee girl.

beats.goal: Ishai burns off the day's adrenaline on the treadmill. Sivan, on the next one, watches 8bitTV on the second screen and comments dryly on his walking pace; they talk for the first time properly. Then Michal by the mirror invites him to her Friday 7am run club, which she herself never shows up to.
beats.teaser: Ishai meets the gym regulars properly. One of them is competitive.
beats.forceText: At Herzl Gym Ishai walks on the treadmill next to Sivan, who runs much faster and watches 8bitTV on the second screen.

forceLines.say: You've been on the walking setting for ten minutes.

forceCommentary.say: Sivan is running like she's late. Ishai is walking like he's early.

moments.text: Herzl Gym in the evening. Ishai walks on a treadmill under the two wall screens: Channel 9 with the weather on the left, 8bitTV's blocky cooking show on the right. On the next treadmill Sivan runs fast, eyes on the right screen.

lines.say: You've been on the walking setting for ten minutes.
It's a strategic walk. I'm warming up.
Your warm-up is longer than my run.
I had a big day. I'm walking it off.
Big day. You put on real trousers?
Partly. Do you always watch the pixel channel?
Channel 9 is just weather and people shouting. 8bitTV is honest.
He's cooking a square egg.
All eggs are square if you're brave.
I'm putting that on a poster.
You'd have to pay me. Speed it up. Four point five.

commentary.say: Finally Ishai has a gym rival. She doesn't know it, he doesn't know it, I know it.
A square egg on 8bitTV. Finally, a show at Ishai's pace.

moments.text: Ishai raises the speed and starts to jog, breathing hard. Sivan glances at his display, then at her own, and quietly raises hers too.

lines.say: Five. I'm at five. Look.
I saw. I'm at eleven. Don't look.
Is this a race? Nobody said it was a race.
Everything here is a race. The man by the mirror is racing himself.
I'm Ishai, by the way. From across the street.
Sivan. I know. The guy with the husky.
He's a Siberian... something. He's at home.
Good. He'd beat you.
Probably. He has four legs. That's cheating.
No excuses on the treadmill. Only numbers.
Funny. I said a number today too. It went well.
Then say six. Go on.

commentary.say: She knows the dog, not the man. Falafel's fame grows.
Number six, Ishai. You've been training for this all day.

update.memory: Ishai, the guy with the husky from across the street, walked ten minutes and called it a warm-up. Then managed six. Has potential. Too slow.

moments.text: Ishai steps off the treadmill, red-faced, and drinks from the fountain by the mirror, where Michal stretches with one foot on the bar.

lines.say: First time I see you run. Not walk. Run.
Sivan made me. I think I'm dying a little.
Good dying. Come to my Friday run club. Seven in the morning, by the park.
Seven? On a Friday? How many people come?
Very many. Usually. In theory.
How many came last Friday?
...I had a thing. But the group is strong!
Do you go to your own run club, Michal?
I go spiritually. Every Friday. Spiritually.
Then I'll come spiritually too. Same time.
Deal. Don't tell Sivan, she'll come for real.

commentary.say: A run club with no runners. That's not a club, that's a WhatsApp group.
Michal attends spiritually. Like me, at this job.

update.memory: The friendly guy with the dog finally ran. I invited him to the Friday run club. He said he'd come spiritually, like me.

beats.goal: Tomer phones while Ishai is home with Falafel. He wants the presentation story and can't believe Ishai named a price. He reminds him of Thursday's beer and mentions a poster at the park for a band at the old Pump House on Wednesday, 'Penguins something'. Nobody commits.
beats.teaser: Tomer calls, and he's seen a poster about penguins
beats.forceText: Ishai lies on the bed with the phone on his chest, Falafel beside him, as Tomer shouts happily on speaker.

forceLines.say: You said a NUMBER? Ishai habibi, who are you?

forceCommentary.say: Tomer's volume could light the hallway without the fitting.

moments.text: Ishai lies on the bed in a t-shirt, the phone on speaker on his chest. Falafel is stretched out at his feet. Tomer's voice fills the room.

lines.say: Ishai habibi! So? Did the chickpea get married?
It went fine. She loved it. And she wanted it to wink.
To wink? Like a chickpea with a secret?
Exactly that. And I said yes, and it costs extra.
You said a NUMBER? Out loud? To Gadi?
Twelve hundred. He said eight. We ended at a thousand.
I bet you forty shekels you said sorry first.
Almost. I said 'oh, sorry, I didn't'... then I stopped.
Almost doesn't count. You owe me nothing. You owe me a beer.
Thursday. After the class. I remember.

commentary.say: Tomer's turning his best friend's breakthrough into a bet. Iconic.
Chickpea with a secret. That's my memoir title.

moments.text: Ishai sits up and rubs Falafel's ears while Tomer talks fast; outside the window the street lights are on.

lines.say: Wait. I walked through the park today. There's a poster at the old pump house.
The Pump House. Hagit's place. What's on?
Wednesday. Some band. Penguins... something. Penguins Can't Fly?
Penguins can Fly. I saw the board. It says LIVE.
Penguins can't fly, Ishai. It's science.
Maybe that's the point. Like a chickpea that winks.
Are you going? You're going. You go everywhere now.
I don't know. I have files due Wednesday night.
Files, files. Ask me Wednesday. Maybe I come, maybe I sleep.
That's the most Tomer answer possible.
Thank you! Go to sleep, mister thousand shekels.

commentary.say: Penguins can Fly, Wednesday at the Pump House. Somebody book Ishai a date.
Tomer arguing with a band name. Science has never been louder.

update.memory: Ishai named a price to Gadi and got a thousand extra for a winking chickpea. Still owes me Thursday's beer. Told him about the penguin band at the Pump House Wednesday.

hosts: Monday, Sigd today. Ishai's big holiday is a chickpea on a video call.
Rain's gone. Today the only storm is Gadi.
Blue shirt alert. Noa's orders, followed to the letter.
Ten o'clock. Laptop. Chickpea. Our boy against the client.
He rehearsed to the basil last night. Moshe gave notes.
Falafel under the desk: the world's fluffiest footrest.
Somewhere in this city a chickpea is about to become famous.
If Ishai says sorry on that call, I'm drinking. Coffee. It's Monday.
A pressed shirt above, pyjamas below. The video-call uniform.
Gadi has never said thank you first. Never. We checked.
Lunch at Avi's is a ritual. Today it might be a party.
Avi's proverbs: fifty percent wisdom, fifty percent amba.
Noa is staring at her phone like it owes her money.
Cold and clear out there. Jacket weather, Tel Aviv style. Twelve degrees and panic.
The hallway light still works. Tomer, we salute you.
Mrs. Levi's game show is at seven thirty. She shouts the answers. Wrong ones.
The gym tonight: treadmills, mirrors and a man in denial.
Sivan, next treadmill, runs like she's being chased by a deadline.
Michal by the mirror is very motivated. About other people.
Moshe is standing taller today. I'm not crying, Oren's crying.
Oren, you can't name the sprout. — I can. I haven't yet. Out of respect.
Dana's number is in his phone. The photo waits. One week. The man has rules.
Wednesday at the Pump House: a band called Penguins can Fly. Be there.
Thursday: improv lesson two. Yael doesn't know what's coming. Neither does he.
Tomorrow at eleven: Dr. Sasson and the War of Jenkins' Ear. Yes, an ear.
A thousand-word day for a man who usually says three.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, Monday morning, and the sky has finally stopped crying on us.
Twelve degrees in Tel Aviv. Wear a jacket, say you're freezing, you've earned it.
Good Sigd to everyone celebrating, from Jerusalem to Herzl Street.
If you have a big meeting today: breathe, drink water, and don't apologise for existing.
Traffic on the coastal road, but traffic on the coastal road is a state of being.
Caller says her cat learned to open the fridge. Madam, that's not a cat, that's a tenant.
Coming up: songs for people pretending to work from home.
Lunchtime! Falafel is not a meal, it's a philosophy. Discuss.
Clear night tonight. Look up. Stars, satellites, maybe your neighbour's drone.
Wednesday the old Pump House in the park has live music. Tickets at Hagit's window.
The gym called. It misses you. It says it's not angry, just disappointed.
Radio Herzl, still here, still slightly out of tune, like all of us.

zelig: Eleven pigeons yesterday. Twelve today. One is a spy.
The pond is lower by one finger. Someone drinks it at night.
The rain left. It always leaves on Mondays.
A blue shirt walked by. Shirts know things.
michal: Friday, seven o'clock. Everyone's coming. Probably.
Three more sets. Then three more. Then maybe.
lior: A velvet chair or a leather one. This changes everything.
The detective sighs. No. The detective breathes.
kobi: Monday numbers are lucky numbers. Ask anyone.
Seven, fourteen, twenty-two. The machine will learn.
Another one, and then I go. Truly.

street: ...he said Sigd, I said what, he explained for an hour...
...the roof leaks only when it rains, so technically...
...a falafel at eleven is breakfast, at one it's lunch...
...my boss writes 'small thing' and I know my weekend is gone...
market: ...the clementines are back, finally, real winter...
...don't buy the first tomato you see, it's a trap...
...my mother says sweet potato, I say sweet potato is a lie...
...forty shekels for spices? For that I want a story...
park: ...the puddles are bigger than the pond today...
...he runs every day and still looks at me like that...
...is that poster about penguins? at the pump house?...
...the duck is fine, the duck is always fine...
cafe: ...so I told him the deadline was flexible and he believed me...
...an oat flat white, but not too oat...
...I'm writing a novel too, everyone here is...
...the barista drew something on my cup, is that a leaf...

chat.say: Good morning. The hallway light is fixed. Thanks to apt 4's friend. Invoice to the committee? None.
The electrician did it for rugelach. The committee should learn.
Roofer's son came. He said 'interesting' three times and left.
Who leaves wet umbrellas in the stairwell? It's a lake.
Good Sigd to Tsega in building 12. She brought me injera last year. Very good.
Anyone in the building play cards? Asking for a friend. The friend is me.
My show starts in five minutes. If you hear shouting, it's the contestants' fault.
Reminder: the building fee for November. Some of you know who you are.
